geometry_edits.rationale: Make the primary solid read as one continuous bent bar with clearer hierarchy.
Expand the carved void to create a more legible public court at ground level.
Align the public opening with the access edge.

graph_edits.rationale: Strengthen the dominant bent gesture so the whole object reads as one continuous mass rather than a bar plus detached fragment.
Increase curvature slightly to create a clearer continuous primary mass and improve hierarchy.
Preserve and clarify the public threshold toward the verified access side so the frontage reads as a deliberate open edge rather than a sealed face.
Broaden the carved public void so it becomes a usable court/entry seam with stronger ground consequence.

rationale: The candidate is a coherent bent-bar/canyon idea in some views, but it is visually read as a thin, mostly extruded bar with a secondary upright fragment rather than a robust mixed-use neighborhood building. The dominant gesture is legible in top and front, yet the mass fractures across views and the support element feels disconnected. The blue access edge is not convincingly answered by a public void or entry seam; instead the form stays semantically sealed to the frontage. The section logic is especially weak for the stated program: there is no clear active ground threshold, no meaningful terrace/court, and the roof/section do not add a believable program hierarchy. The geometry is repairable and not visibly illegal-clipped, so repair integrity is high, but program fit fails because the visible massing does not sufficiently support neighborhood living with active edge and public space.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Much taller tower typology than the candidate; useful only for upper-mass articulation, not for the low bent-bar composition.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Tapered, stepped vertical massing can support a mixed-use presence when it remains one legible primary figure.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Predominantly tower language; candidate is low and bar-like, so the vertical precedent is only weakly transferable.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A single dominant tower can still read as civic/mixed-use when the profile is continuous and coherent.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference is small horizontal commercial building; candidate lacks an equally legible active ground condition.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A clear ground threshold, canopy/entry seam, and compact public frontage strengthen neighborhood-scale programs.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Counterfactual is more spatially integrated and continuous than the candidate; do not copy the building, only the court/terrace logic.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Courtyard/void plus terraced continuity can turn neighborhood massing into a usable public figure.

warnings: Visible mass is coherent only partially; the upright fragment reads as a separate piece in some views.
Road frontage response is weak: access edge is present but not converted into a legible public void or threshold.
Section lacks a convincing neighborhood-living ground/public relationship.
Non-stair silhouette is not the issue here; the issue is insufficient void/public logic and weak primary mass.
